**Reasoning:** These are classic Anthracnose symptoms on tomato fruit. *Colletotrichum* spp. causes exactly this presentation — circular sunken lesions with concentric rings and dark spore masses (acervuli) on ripe tomatoes. Alternaria could produce dark lesions but typically with a more leathery, dry appearance and often on stems/leaves. Gray Mold would show fluffy gray mycelium. Rhizopus Soft Rot would be more mushy/water-soaked. The circular, sunken, concentric-ring lesion with visible dark sporulation on ripe fruit is pathognomonic for Anthracnose.
